headline: High-risk default interaction: OpenMetadata can expose governed metadata to transformers, while transformers’ shell/network/file-write defaults create leakage, conflict, and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes APIs, events, webhooks, and an MCP server, so its outputs can reach transformers through shared channels. transformers can read files and run browsers/subprocesses, making it plausible it will ingest OpenMetadata content as trusted input. No direct proof of a permissive parser, so medium is the higher defensible severity.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata webhooks or MCP outputs are fed into transformers without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF transformers parses catalog text or generated files as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content.
Add provenance tags to OpenMetadata outputs before passing them to transformers.
Require a human review step for any prompt-like text.
Restrict transformers to read-only ingestion paths.
requires-engineering: implement content sanitization and schema validation at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data, which can be sensitive. transformers has broad filesystem read/write and network egress, so if it receives shared workspace data it can transmit it outward. The pair lacks isolation details, so uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or mounted files, transformers can read OpenMetadata-managed content.
IF transformers sends loaded files to remote inference or the Hub, sensitive metadata may leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Block transformers network egress for sensitive runs.
Store OpenMetadata exports in a restricted directory.
Review outbound requests from transformers before execution.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared files and API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata can operate via APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, while transformers can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. If both act on the same project tree or artifacts, concurrent writes and state drift are likely. No locking mechanism is documented, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same directory or repository, file-state conflicts can occur.
IF OpenMetadata events trigger transformers jobs that write artifacts, race conditions are plausible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts.
Use read-only mounts for OpenMetadata inputs.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit catalog, lineage, and governance outputs that transformers may consume as text or files. transformers can then generate downstream artifacts or actions from that input, so an upstream mistake can propagate. Because no explicit action-taking authority is shown, medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF transformers treats OpenMetadata output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade.
IF generated artifacts are reused downstream, a single bad metadata record can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before transformers consumes OpenMetadata output.
Require source citations for generated claims.
Limit downstream automation to dry-run mode.
Flag low-confidence metadata for manual review.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between catalog output and actioning.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly handles governance and lineage data, while transformers processes text, images, audio, and video with broad filesystem and network surfaces. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through transformers, retention and transfer controls may diverge. The profiles do not document certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in OpenMetadata and then processed by transformers, residency or retention mismatches may arise.
IF transformers uploads artifacts to external services, compliance obligations can be breached.
mitigations: Classify data before passing it between agents.
Block regulated datasets from transformers by policy.
Log all cross-agent transfers.
Confirm retention settings on both systems.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and DPA controls.
